correctness.rationale: For \(p\ge5\) the integer polynomial \(D_p\) reduces to \(X^p\)  modulo \(p\). Its derivative divided by \(p\) reduces to \((X^2-4)^{(p-1)/2}\), giving valuation-one contraction on all noncritical classes. At \(\pm2\) the derivative is \(p^2\), the second Taylor coefficient has \(p^2\) and other higher Taylor coefficients have required \(p\)-divisibility, giving the exact \(p^3\) normalized branch isometry. The scaled unit-linear bijections compose because \(D_p\) is identity  modulo \(p\), proving every ball, modulus-\(p^k\) fiber, Haar measure, least input period, and collision count. Exact independent modular checker passed 170481 value checks and 4680 distance assertions; finite checks are diagnostic.

originality.rationale: Direct full-text comparison with Bremser–Gomez-Calderon 1991 confirms that generic noncritical fiber counts are known, whereas the critical \(\pm2\) branch only has bounds in Theorem 11. This claim supplies exact ball equalities and all critical fiber counts for \(D_{p^r}\) at \(p\ge5\), with iteration and least-period laws. Gassert 2012 treats finite fields and Panraksa–Tangboonduangjit 2026 periodic points, not full finite-level value sets. No explicit equivalent was located in published research records; implicit older equivalence remains a priority risk.
residual_risks: An implicit result in a general work on ramified Galois-ring polynomial maps may specialize to the exact claimed balls without naming Dickson polynomials.

value.rationale: The previously unresolved critical-residue portion of the natural Dickson degree-p^r value-set problem has a complete explicit classification, closing the remaining gap left by the 1991 upper/lower value-set estimates in a uniform family. Exact critical images and fibers resolve integer congruence representability, collision counts, Haar measure and additive periods at every prime-power precision, not merely a routine isolated numerical example.
